messages:
cs_taylor: FYI ACME reported a spike of 503s ~15:02 UTC. They attached a short log showing upstream worker exit during a toolcall — 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)'. Customer-facing impact: batch requests failing, retries visible in their logs.
alert_bot: [ALERT] hosted-infer upstream-worker exit on infer-3g-21 (code 139). 120 failures in 3m. Links: https://monitoring.internal/alerts/1759991111, logs: /var/log/upstream/infer-3g-21/exit.log
mike_oncall: Ack. Jumping in. Can someone paste the last 200 lines of the worker log and dmesg around the time? Any gpu-reset/nvml messages?
cs_taylor: Pasted cropped logs from customer and our host: 
```
[runtime] toolcall: spawned subprocess pid=8642
[kv-prefetch] prefetch batch=128 mem=2.3GB
*** SIGSEGV received at 0x00000000 ***
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
nvml: GPU 0: GPU has fallen off the bus
InferRunner exited with code 139
```
mike_oncall: nvml reset + bad_alloc combo — could be GPU OOM cascade or memory corruption during prefetch. Amanda, any recent prefetch/kv-cache changes rolled yesterday?
amanda_runtime: I pushed a small prefetch tweak in staging yesterday to increase parallel prefetch windows (PR #3421) — might increase pinned host memory briefly. But that alone shouldn't cause nvml reset. Looking at the crashline it aborts after std::bad_alloc then segfaults. Suspect cross-device memory thrash + cuda driver reset.
ops_jay: Host eject logs show a driver reset around the same time: `dmesg` snippet -> "NVRM: GPU at 0000:3a:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus" and then container OOM killer invoked.
sre_bot: Autoscaler note: infer-3g-21 had a transient spike of 60% CPU/85% GPU mem within 30s before exit, then container restart loop x2. Routing fallback triggered for 30s.
mike_oncall: Next steps: 1) capture full core + gdb stack, 2) check nvml/nvidia-smi timeline, 3) attempt quick mitigation for customer (route to fallback pool or downgrade to smaller model). Amanda, can you share repro steps we can run on a repro host?
amanda_runtime: Repro recipe I used locally that hit a similar crash: heavy toolcall combining a long prompt (12k tokens) + large prefetch window + quant swap enabled. Steps:
```bash
# on repro host with same runtime build
export MODEL=redwood/giant-13b-quant
export PREFETCH_THREADS=8
./run_infer --model $MODEL --prefetch-window 128 --enable-quant-swap 
# then invoke a toolcall that returns a ~8MB payload in streaming mode
curl -X POST https://local-infer/run -d '{"prompt": "<long prompt>", "toolcall": true}'
```
When I hit it, driver reported mem spike then reset. I was able to reproduce after 4-5 runs.
cs_lead: Customer wants ETA and mitigation. Can we do a traffic split to Dedicated fallback for ACME while we triage?
mike_oncall: I enabled a temporary rule to route ACME traffic to dedicated-fallback for 10m. Monitoring — please confirm customer sees fewer 503s. :white_check_mark:
cs_taylor: CS says errors dropped after routing. They still see occasional latency spikes but no hard 503s for the last 6m. Thanks.
amanda_runtime: For triage I'll pull core and run gdb. Please run these on the node (requires root):
```bash
sudo cp /var/crash/core.infer-3g-21 /tmp/core.infer
sudo gdb -ex "thread apply all bt full" -ex quit /opt/bin/infer_runner /tmp/core.infer > /tmp/core_bt.txt
sudo nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv -lms 100 --display=brief &> /tmp/nvml_timeline.log &
```
mike_oncall: Copying logs now. Also grabbing container inspect and runtime env. Any quick mitigation to prevent recurrence?
amanda_runtime: Short term: 1) rollback prefetch PR on hosts serving high-QPS toolcalls, 2) disable quant-swap rollouts for this model family (it adds memory churn), 3) add a safety cap on prefetch-window for hosted pools. I'll open follow-up tickets.
sre_bot: Note added to incident: INC-1759991111. Autoscaler prevented wider blast by moving some pods.
ops_jay: I uploaded host-level dmesg and /var/log/nvidia-driver.log to the incident folder: https://internal.artifacts/1759991111/host-logs.tar.gz
cs_taylor: Thanks all. CS confirmed routing fix improved customer experience. Amanda — please paste gdb output when ready. We'll keep ACME on dedicated-fallback until final mitigation. :pray:
